A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures and Appendix A support reliable comparison across layout changes and figure renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original English-to-Dutch translation experiments, classifier accuracies, reward-component ablations and hyperparameter experiments in Section 6 and Tables 2–5.

after.justification: V2 retains the original empirical experiments and reports additional baseline results and cross-classifier evaluations in Table 2 and Figure 3.

M1.justification: The MT architecture, three BERTje classifiers, thresholded naturalness and COMET rewards, harmonic-mean combination, and mixed supervised/reward objective remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 and Equations 1–6 retain the same procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Dutch monolingual data and 531 English-to-Dutch parallel books, including the same 31 test novels in Appendix A.1. The added classifier evaluations reuse existing HT, MT and OR data and tasks.

E2.justification: V2 adds Tailored RR (Top-k) as an evaluated comparator in Section 5.1 and Table 2; v1 only discussed this work. The base MT model, APE and both Tagging configurations remain.

E3.justification: V2 adds a protocol evaluating each classifier on all three existing binary test sets (Figure 3). Its replacement checkpoint curves explicitly use validation data; v1 did not separately identify that figure's split. Corpus splits, translation metrics, training settings and the final 5K checkpoint remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The new classifier evaluation matrix examines transfer across classification tasks. Figure 2 also adds validation-loss traces supporting the existing analysis of loss versus naturalness. Reward ablations, the beta=0 experiment, translation example and per-book analysis are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages over test books without repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals or significance tests. V2's additional curves and classifier matrix do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Supporting results change: HT-OR/MT-HT/MT-OR classifier accuracies move from 84.8/78.2/91.1 to 65.8/77.4/81.2, reversing the first two classifiers' ranking. V2 adds cross-test results and Tailored RR scores, including MTLD 104.3 and MetricX 4.86, and replaces Figure 2's curves with explicitly validation-set results. Shared Table 2 scores and Tables 3 and 5 remain identical; Section 6.5 adds previously omitted MTLD exceptions.

T1.justification: The mathematical objectives, reward definitions and lexical-diversity formula remain unchanged. Neither version contains additional theoretical propositions or proofs; the expanded metric explanations do not introduce new mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claim: multi-perspective alignment improves lexical richness and naturalness without sacrificing translation accuracy in English-to-Dutch literary translation.

C2.justification: V2 newly justifies prioritizing MTLD over TTR and Yule's I through its stability across text lengths. It also qualifies the loss–naturalness mismatch to some models after 1K steps. The proposed reward-mismatch explanation and substantive limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-repository pointer in the introduction and states that preliminary results informed the reward thresholds. It also identifies the computing cluster in acknowledgments. Existing implementation settings and Appendix A's reproducibility details are retained; the linked code's contents are not established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: V2 adds Lai et al. (2021a) on style transfer without task-specific parallel data and McCarthy and Jarvis (2010) on lexical-diversity measurement. These extend methodological motivation and metric justification without substantially changing the paper's positioning.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized revisions to related work, metric explanations and results discussion, and moves classifier-performance reporting from methodology into a separate results paragraph. It also updates author affiliations and adds acknowledgments. The overall narrative and section sequence remain recognizable.

P2.justification: V2 adds the classifier heatmap, introduces a loss axis and series in Figure 2, and enlarges the existing per-book plot from one column to full width. It also adds the Tailored RR table row, resizes Figure 1 and adjusts captions and table placement. Appendix displays remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The added Tailored RR comparison, classifier diagnostics, explicit validation/loss plots and code pointer modestly strengthen evaluation and documentation. Larger plots and the rationale for prioritizing MTLD improve interpretability. The core method and translation results remain unchanged, and v2 does not explain the revised classifier accuracies, limiting the gain in empirical transparency.
